newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Hartmann says assumes punctual EMU start.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Hartmann says assumes punctual EMU start.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Wendelin Hartmann said on Monday that he assumed that European monetary union would start on time in 1999 and include Germany.

In the opening remarks of a speech about the effect of monetary union on Germany as a financial centre -- which concentrated on technicalities of the changeover period -- Hartmann outlined the timetable for the transition to the euro.
"You can tell from my introductory remarks that I am assuming that Germany will meet the economic framework conditions and as a result will take part in the third stage on January 1, 1999," he said.
A text of his speech was released in advance of delivery.

Turning to the issue of payment systems within monetary union, Hartmann noted that there had been a dispute among central banks over whether a country which did not join EMU should gain full access to the TARGET gross payment system.

Hartmann reiterated the Bundesbank's opposition to the idea of full access for non-EMU European Union countries, saying that even an offer of intraday credit in the system to such countries raised the prospect of them holding overnight credits.
The Bundesbank has argued in the past that such overnight credits could pose a theoretical risk to the smooth conduct of monetary policy within monetary union.
